title: The Three Round Table Conferences
definition: A series of three peace conferences organized by the British Government between 1930 and 1932 to discuss constitutional reforms in India, following the failure of the Simon Commission.
importanceInUpsc: These conferences are central to understanding the transition from the Civil Disobedience Movement to the Government of India Act, 1935, and the evolution of the communal award.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of The Three Round Table Conferences.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
